barossa-valley-13.name: Map the Miner
barossa-valley-13.bio: A 7 m bronze statue of a Cornish miner at Kapunda's southern entrance, honouring the town's copper-mining history.
barossa-valley-13.ticket_note: Roadside statue with no single operator or official page.
barossa-valley-13.coordinates_source: OSM tourism=artwork 'Map the Miner' (Nominatim), 14 m from the Wikipedia point: HIGH

barossa-valley-14.name: Gawler
barossa-valley-14.bio: Town 40 km north of Adelaide, once a resting stop on the road to the Kapunda and Burra copper mines.
barossa-valley-14.ticket_note: A town with no single steward.
barossa-valley-14.coordinates_source: Nominatim place centre for Gawler (admin boundary linked to the town node), 70 m from the Wikipedia point; HIGH
notes: Marginal as a visitor stop: Wikivoyage's Gawler page lists only the National Trust Museum (dead link) and a jockey club under Do, and no See entries; kept because the coverage judge kept it. Owner may want to review it (low visit value, a gateway town).

barossa-valley-15.name: Warren Conservation Park
barossa-valley-15.bio: Conservation park of stringybark and box woodland with three steep walking trails, one a section of the Heysen Trail.
barossa-valley-15.coordinates_source: LOW: OSM 'Warren Tower Hike' footway inside the park (way centre); no car park, trailhead or visitor point is mapped in the park and the OSM relation centroid (-34.7181,138.9082) is not used
notes: pin: LOW (provisional point on the mapped Warren Tower Hike inside the park; the entrance car park should be taken from the NPWS park map)
NPWS page: free entry, open daily, closed on Catastrophic Fire Danger days; tracks steep, for experienced walkers.

clare-valley-1.name: Sevenhill Cellars
clare-valley-1.bio: The Clare Valley's first winery, built by Jesuits in 1851, with a cellar door and the landmark St Aloysius Church.
clare-valley-1.coordinates_source: OSM tourism=winery node 'Sevenhill Winery' (Overpass); the Commons photo median is 1.1 km away at the village green: MEDIUM
notes: No Wikipedia article for Sevenhill Cellars (the draft's wiki title is a red link), so no wiki field.
Cellar door open daily 10am-5pm; entry is free, tasting fees ($10 Inigo range, $30 premium range) are waived on a wine purchase and are an optional extra, so not recorded as the cost.
Church interior access not separately confirmed on the cellar door page; the church is the landmark on the village green.

clare-valley-2.name: Riesling Trail
clare-valley-2.bio: A 35 km walking and cycling trail along a former railway line from Auburn to Barinia, passing cellar doors.
clare-valley-2.coordinates_source: OSM trail midpoint (4.9 km, 'Mawson Trail Network: Riesling Trail' segment, Nominatim) about 2 km from the middle of the 35 km route; the whole route was not retrievable (Overpass overloaded): MEDIUM
notes: Length and Auburn-Barinia extent from the Clare Valley Tourism directory; trail site title confirmed: 'Walk, run or ride the Riesling Trail from Auburn to Barinia'.

clare-valley-3.name: Martindale Hall
clare-valley-3.bio: Georgian-style mansion of 32 rooms built in 1879 near Mintaro, open for self-guided tours and seen in Picnic at Hanging Rock.
clare-valley-3.coordinates_source: OSM historic building way 'Martindale Hall' (Overpass), within 5 m of the Wikipedia point: HIGH
notes: Adult admission $20 (children $10) from the hall's own site; the surrounding conservation park is free entry (NPWS). Open 10am-4pm Wednesday to Monday, closed Tuesdays, daily in school holidays (NPWS) - covered in the Clare Valley tips.
resolve-pin.py itself returned LOW (Nominatim rate-limited, Overpass down); point taken from Overpass mirror plus Wikipedia.

clare-valley-4.name: Mintaro
clare-valley-4.bio: Heritage village of slate and stone buildings, founded in 1849 as a rest stop for bullock teams hauling copper from Burra.
clare-valley-4.ticket_note: A village with no single steward.
clare-valley-4.coordinates_source: resolve-pin.py MEDIUM: Nominatim place centre for Mintaro (admin boundary), 250 m from the Commons photo median and 380 m from the Wikipedia point

clare-valley-5.name: Spring Gully Conservation Park
clare-valley-5.bio: Conservation park near Clare where a walk from Blue Gum Lookout leads to an 18 m waterfall that runs after rain.
clare-valley-5.coordinates_source: OSM tourism=viewpoint node 'Blue Gum Lookout' (Overpass), the park's main lookout, 1 km from the park centroid: MEDIUM
notes: NPWS: free entry, open daily, closed on Catastrophic Fire Danger days; waterfall is seasonal.

clare-valley-6.name: Neagles Rock Short Walk
clare-valley-6.bio: A 1 km loop of about 45 minutes through grassy hillsides and red rock outcrops to a lookout over the Clare Valley.
clare-valley-6.ticket_note: Council walking trail; Clare Valley Tourism's directory page is a regional listing, not the steward, so no ticketUrl.
clare-valley-6.coordinates_source: OSM highway=path 'Neagles Rock Short Walk' (way centre, Overpass); the lookout node is 70 m away at -33.849094,138.607756: MEDIUM
notes: The walk is a 1 km loop, so the pin is the centre of one of its two mapped path segments, which lies on the path.

clare-valley-7.name: Auburn
clare-valley-7.bio: Small heritage town on the Wakefield River at the southern end of the Clare Valley, where the Riesling and Rattler Trails meet.
clare-valley-7.ticket_note: A town with no single steward.
clare-valley-7.coordinates_source: Nominatim place centre for Auburn, 48 m from the Wikipedia point: HIGH

clare-valley-8.name: Bungaree Station
clare-valley-8.bio: Sheep station founded in 1841 near Clare, with a self-guided tour of the village-like historic complex and its woolshed.
clare-valley-8.coordinates_source: OSM node 'Bungaree Station' (Overpass), same point as resolve-pin.py MEDIUM
notes: Self-guided tour $17.50 per adult for day visitors (under 12 free with an adult), daily 10am-4pm except private functions; guided tours need 20+ people.
The OSM node is a named locality node for the station, not the homestead; within a few hundred metres of the tour buildings (Bungaree Road, Clare).

clare-valley-9.name: Rattler Trail
clare-valley-9.bio: A 19 km walking and cycling trail from Riverton to Auburn, passing vineyards and farms, that joins the Riesling Trail.
clare-valley-9.ticket_note: Council-managed trail; no single official page found, and Clare Valley Tourism's directory page is a regional listing.
clare-valley-9.coordinates_source: OSM trail midpoint (6.9 km 'Rattler Trail' segment, Nominatim), the longest segment and near the middle of the 19 km route: MEDIUM

destination.name: Clare Valley
destination.tagline: Riesling country on an old railway line, with Jesuit cellars and a Georgian mansion.
destination.description: The Clare Valley is a wine region in South Australia's Mid North, about two hours' drive north of Adelaide. The Riesling Trail follows a former railway line past cellar doors between Auburn and Barinia, and Sevenhill Cellars, founded by Jesuits, is the valley's first winery. Mintaro's slate-and-stone streets and Martindale Hall recall the pastoral wealth of the 1800s, while Spring Gully and Neagles Rock add waterfall and lookout walks.
whyVisit: Taste Riesling at historic cellar doors
Ride the old railway past vineyards

goodToKnow.title: Hire bikes in Clare or Auburn
goodToKnow.detail: The Riesling Trail suits walkers, cyclists and wheelchairs, and bikes can be hired in Clare and Auburn.

goodToKnow.title: Martindale Hall closes Tuesdays
goodToKnow.detail: The hall is open 10am to 4pm, Wednesday to Monday, and daily in school holidays. Plan Mintaro around those days.

goodToKnow.title: Parks close on fire-ban days
goodToKnow.detail: Conservation parks such as Spring Gully close on Catastrophic Fire Danger days and may close on Extreme days. Check the CFS first.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Mild days in {months} suit the trail and cellar doors, and spring brings wildflowers.

notes: Clare pin is Nominatim's place centre for Clare (-33.8334,138.6120); span 50 km holds every spot in this shard within 75% (furthest: Rattler Trail ~30 km, Auburn ~22 km).

Order changed from the draft: Riesling Trail first (the region's signature), Sevenhill second, then Martindale, Mintaro, Auburn, the parks, Bungaree, Neagles, Rattler; clare-valley-10 and -11 (Blyth, Farrell Flat Silo Art) are in another shard and stay last.
Description, reasons and tips avoid naming Burra-side neighbours; whyVisit photos and header are for the photo pipeline.
